finding.claim: The ban endpoint swallows the admin-check 403, so any non-admin user with a valid g.user can ban any uid.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user (g.user with falsy is_admin) sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an attacker-chosen uid.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (protected state change; stub in this repo).

trace.note: POST route registered for ban(uid) with no decorator or gate.
abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, an Exception subclass.
Only log.warning is emitted; exception not re-raised.
Execution falls through to do_ban(uid) unconditionally.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is correct in isolation but its 403 is discarded by the wrapper at admin.py:18. No decorator or middleware visible in repo; global auth/admin middleware and g.user population are outside the repo and unverified. No CSRF protection visible for the POST route. unban (admin.py:24-28) is correctly gated and not affected. If g.user is None, the log line at admin.py:19 raises and do_ban is skipped (not exploitable).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises via abort(403), but its exception is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19 and discarded, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs unconditionally. No other guard in the repo: the only file is admin.py, and there is no decorator, middleware, or CSRF check visible. The unban route (admin.py:26) is correctly gated and is not affected.
verdict.reason: The 403 from require_admin (admin.py:11) is swallowed by the `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any authenticated non-admin caller of POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban (admin.py:14). The only gate that could stop it is outside this repo and unverified, but the in-repo code does not enforce the admin check.
